newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end flat, further rises seen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end flat, further rises seen.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporate bonds closed flat on Wednesday for the third consecutive sesssion, but dealers said fears about a money squeeze would push up the benchmark yield further.
A repo issue by the central bank had no impact on the market.
* 3-yr corporates end unchanged at Tuesday's 12.70. * 3-mth CDs close at 12.95 against 12.75.
The Hongkong Bank dealer said trading was thin as investors appeared reluctant to buy bonds.
But shorter-term yields continued to rise, reflecting worries about tightening liquidity.
The one-week call rate was quoted at 13.50-13.80, and three-month commercial papers hit an intraday high of 13.40/50.
"It is mirroring a typical liquidity tightness," said the Hyundai Securities dealer.
The central bank supplied 800 billion won to the local banking system through repurchase agreements but the market was unfazed by the Repo issue. -Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
